description: The commands that create new geometry and annotation objects: lines, curves, polylines, hatches and regions, text and tables, blocks and attributes, and the parametric constraints that hold a sketch together. Every one can be typed at the command prompt, put in a script or macro, or called from AutoLISP with (command "_LINE" ...).

tools.name: LINE
tools.description: Draw a series of independent straight line segments. Each segment is a separate LINE object even though they are drawn in one continuous operation, which is the key difference from PLINE. Press Enter at the first point prompt to start from the end of the last line or arc drawn, and use Close to return to the first point.
tools.usage:
LINE  (alias L)
Specify first point: <point>
Specify next point or [Undo]: <point>
Specify next point or [Close/Undo]: C | U | Enter

parameters.name: Close (C)
parameters.description: Join the last point back to the first and end the command.

parameters.name: Undo (U)
parameters.description: Remove the last segment drawn without leaving the command.

parameters.name: Enter at first prompt
parameters.description: Continue from the endpoint of the most recently drawn line or arc.

parameters.name: @dx,dy
parameters.description: Relative rectangular coordinates; @dist<angle gives relative polar coordinates.

tools.example:
; Script form - draw a 100 x 50 rectangle from four lines
LINE
0,0
100,0
100,50
0,50
C

; AutoLISP form
(command "_LINE" '(0 0) '(100 0) '(100 50) '(0 50) "_C")
tools.notes: Use PLINE when the result should behave as one object (for offsetting, area calculation or joining). JOIN converts a chain of collinear or connected LINE objects into a single line or polyline.

tools.name: PLINE
tools.description: Draw a 2D polyline: a single object made of connected straight and arc segments that can carry a global or per-segment width. Because it is one object it can be offset, filleted as a whole, joined, given an area and perimeter by the LIST command, and extruded into a solid. Switch between line and arc modes inside the command with the Arc and Line options.
tools.usage:
PLINE  (alias PL)
Specify start point: <point>
Specify next point or [Arc/Halfwidth/Length/Undo/Width]: <point> | A | H | L | U | W
(in Arc mode) [Angle/CEnter/CLose/Direction/Halfwidth/Line/Radius/Second pt/Undo/Width]

parameters.name: Arc (A)
parameters.description: Switch to arc segments; Line (L) switches back.

parameters.name: Width (W)
parameters.description: Set the starting and ending width of the next segment, which is how tapered arrows and leaders are drawn.

parameters.name: Halfwidth (H)
parameters.description: Same as Width but specified from the centre line outwards.

parameters.name: Length (L)
parameters.description: Continue in the same direction as the previous segment for a given length.

parameters.name: Close (C)
parameters.description: Close the polyline back to the start point, creating a closed loop with a proper vertex.

tools.example:
; Tapered arrow drawn as a single polyline
PLINE
0,0
W
0
0
50,0
W
6
0
60,0


; AutoLISP: closed triangle
(command "_PLINE" '(0 0) '(100 0) '(50 80) "_C")
tools.notes: PEDIT edits an existing polyline (width, fit curve, spline, join, open/close). PLINETYPE controls whether new polylines are created as optimised LWPOLYLINE objects (value 2, the default) or legacy heavyweight POLYLINE objects. Closing with C is not the same as drawing back to the start point: only C creates a true closed flag.

tools.name: XLINE
tools.description: Create a construction line that is infinite in both directions. Construction lines are used as layout references: they extend forever so they always intersect what you need, and they are ignored by ZOOM Extents. Draw them on a dedicated non-plotting layer so they never appear in output.
tools.usage:
XLINE  (alias XL)
Specify a point or [Hor/Ver/Ang/Bisect/Offset]: <point> | H | V | A | B | O
Specify through point: <point>

parameters.name: Hor / Ver
parameters.description: Create horizontal or vertical construction lines through picked points.

parameters.name: Ang (A)
parameters.description: Create construction lines at a given angle, optionally referenced to an existing object.

parameters.name: Bisect (B)
parameters.description: Create a line bisecting an angle defined by a vertex and two points.

parameters.name: Offset (O)
parameters.description: Create a construction line parallel to an existing line at a given distance.

tools.example:
; Layout grid of construction lines on a non-plotting layer
-LAYER M CONSTRUCTION P N CONSTRUCTION

XLINE
H
0,0
0,1000
0,2000

XLINE
V
0,0
1500,0
tools.notes: RAY is the same idea but infinite in one direction only. Construction lines are real objects and are saved with the drawing, so purge them or freeze their layer before issuing the drawing.

tools.name: RAY
tools.description: Create a semi-infinite construction line that starts at a point and extends in one direction forever. Use it where an XLINE would clutter the drawing on the unwanted side, for example when projecting features from an elevation into a plan view in one direction only.
tools.usage:
RAY
Specify start point: <point>
Specify through point: <point>
Specify through point: <point> | Enter

parameters.name: start point
parameters.description: The finite end of the ray.

parameters.name: through point
parameters.description: Defines the direction; the command repeats so several rays can share one start point.

tools.notes: Rays and construction lines are trimmed into finite lines by TRIM and BREAK, which is a common way to turn a layout reference into real geometry.

tools.name: POLYGON
tools.description: Draw a regular polygon of 3 to 1024 sides as a closed polyline. The size is given either by a circle the polygon is inscribed in or circumscribed about, or by the length and direction of one edge. Because the result is an LWPOLYLINE it can be offset, filleted and extruded like any other polyline.
tools.usage:
POLYGON  (alias POL)
Enter number of sides <4>: <n>
Specify center of polygon or [Edge]: <point> | E
Enter an option [Inscribed in circle/Circumscribed about circle] <I>: I | C
Specify radius of circle: <radius>

parameters.name: number of sides
parameters.description: 3 to 1024. The last value used is remembered as the default.

parameters.name: Inscribed (I)
parameters.description: Vertices lie on the circle of the given radius (across corners).

parameters.name: Circumscribed (C)
parameters.description: Edge midpoints lie on the circle (across flats) - the option to use for a hex nut given its A/F dimension.

parameters.name: Edge (E)
parameters.description: Define the polygon by the two endpoints of one edge instead of a centre and radius.

tools.example:
; M12 hex nut outline: 19 mm across flats
POLYGON
6
0,0
C
9.5

; Triangle from one edge
POLYGON
3
E
0,0
50,0
tools.notes: Circumscribed uses the across-flats dimension that fastener standards quote; inscribed uses across-corners. Picking the wrong one is the most common mistake when drawing fasteners.

tools.name: RECTANG
tools.description: Draw a rectangular closed polyline from two opposite corners, with options for chamfered or filleted corners, a line width, an elevation and a thickness. The Dimensions and Rotation options let you type the size rather than picking, which is what scripts and macros normally do.
tools.usage:
RECTANG  (alias REC)
Specify first corner point or [Chamfer/Elevation/Fillet/Thickness/Width]: <point>
Specify other corner point or [Area/Dimensions/Rotation]: <point> | A | D | R

parameters.name: Chamfer (C)
parameters.description: Set two chamfer distances applied to all four corners of subsequent rectangles.

parameters.name: Fillet (F)
parameters.description: Set a corner radius applied to all four corners.

parameters.name: Width (W)
parameters.description: Polyline width for the rectangle.

parameters.name: Dimensions (D)
parameters.description: Type length and width instead of picking the second corner.

parameters.name: Rotation (R)
parameters.description: Rotate the rectangle by an angle or by picking two points.

parameters.name: Thickness (T) / Elevation (E)
parameters.description: 3D thickness and Z elevation, which turn the rectangle into an extruded box outline.

tools.example:
; 200 x 120 rectangle with 5 mm filleted corners at the origin
RECTANG
F
5
0,0
D
200
120


; AutoLISP
(command "_RECTANG" "_F" 5.0 '(0 0) "_D" 200.0 120.0 '(1 1))
tools.notes: Chamfer and Fillet settings are sticky: they persist to the next RECTANG until reset to 0. A rectangle is a normal closed polyline, so EXPLODE turns it into four lines.

tools.name: ARC
tools.description: Draw a circular arc using one of eleven combinations of start point, second point, end point, centre, angle, direction, radius and chord length. The default three-point method draws counter-clockwise from the first point through the second to the third; the Centre-based methods always sweep counter-clockwise unless a negative angle is given.
tools.usage:
ARC  (alias A)
Specify start point of arc or [Center]: <point> | C
Specify second point of arc or [Center/End]: <point> | C | E
Specify end point of arc:
(further options: Angle / Direction / Radius / Length of chord)

parameters.name: Center (C)
parameters.description: Define the arc by its centre plus a start point and then an angle, chord length or end point.

parameters.name: End (E)
parameters.description: Give the end point, then choose Angle, Direction, Radius or Centre to resolve the arc.

parameters.name: Angle (A)
parameters.description: Included angle; a negative value sweeps clockwise.

parameters.name: Radius (R)
parameters.description: Arc radius, used with a start and end point.

parameters.name: Direction (D)
parameters.description: Tangent direction at the start point.

tools.example:
; Start, Center, Angle - a 90 degree arc
ARC
100,0
C
0,0
A
90

; Start, End, Radius
ARC
0,0
E
100,0
R
60
tools.notes: Pressing Enter at the first prompt starts an arc tangent to the last line or arc drawn. Arcs are always drawn counter-clockwise in the current UCS unless an option reverses them, which is why arcs sometimes appear on the wrong side; use a negative angle or swap the start and end points.

tools.name: CIRCLE
tools.description: Draw a circle from a centre and radius or diameter, from two or three points on the circumference, or tangent to two or three existing objects. The tangent methods (Ttr and the 3P/Tan Tan Tan variant) are what make it practical to construct fillet geometry and cam profiles without calculating centres by hand.
tools.usage:
CIRCLE  (alias C)
Specify center point for circle or [3P/2P/Ttr (tan tan radius)]: <point> | 3P | 2P | T
Specify radius of circle or [Diameter]: <radius> | D <diameter>

parameters.name: 3P
parameters.description: Three points on the circumference.

parameters.name: 2P
parameters.description: Two points defining the diameter.

parameters.name: Ttr (T)
parameters.description: Tangent to two objects with a specified radius; pick near the intended tangent points because several solutions exist.

parameters.name: Diameter (D)
parameters.description: Enter a diameter instead of a radius.

tools.example:
CIRCLE
50,50
25

; Diameter instead of radius
CIRCLE
150,50
D
40

; Tangent to two lines, radius 10
CIRCLE
T
nea
10,0
nea
0,10
10
tools.notes: A circle drawn with a thickness becomes a cylinder in 3D views. To draw a circle tangent to three objects use the Tan Tan Tan option on the ribbon, which runs CIRCLE 3P with tangent snaps pre-set.

tools.name: ELLIPSE
tools.description: Draw a true ellipse or an elliptical arc from the endpoints of one axis plus a half-length of the other, or from a centre and two axis endpoints. The Rotation option produces the ellipse you get by rotating a circle about its major axis, which is exactly how circular holes appear in isometric views.
tools.usage:
ELLIPSE  (alias EL)
Specify axis endpoint of ellipse or [Arc/Center/Isocircle]: <point> | A | C | I
Specify other endpoint of axis: <point>
Specify distance to other axis or [Rotation]: <dist> | R <angle>

parameters.name: Arc (A)
parameters.description: Create an elliptical arc; you then specify start and end angles or an included angle.

parameters.name: Center (C)
parameters.description: Define by centre point plus one endpoint of each axis.

parameters.name: Rotation (R)
parameters.description: Define the minor axis as a circle rotated about the major axis by the given angle.

parameters.name: Isocircle (I)
parameters.description: Available only when isometric snap is on (SNAP Style Isometric); draws the correct isometric circle in the current isoplane.

tools.example:
; Ellipse with a 100 major axis and 60 minor axis
ELLIPSE
C
0,0
50,0
0,30

; Isometric circle - requires isometric snap
SNAP
S
I
L
ELLIPSE
I
0,0
25
tools.notes: PELLIPSE controls the object type: 0 (default) creates a true ELLIPSE object, 1 creates a polyline approximation, which some downstream systems and older CNC post-processors require.

tools.name: SPLINE
tools.description: Draw a NURBS curve, either by fit points that the curve passes through or by control vertices that pull it into shape. Fit-point splines are easier to draw to known coordinates; CV splines give smoother, more predictable curvature and are what surface modelling expects. Use them for contours, cams, road centrelines and any smooth profile that arcs cannot express.
tools.usage:
SPLINE  (alias SPL)
Current settings: Method=Fit  Knots=Chord
Specify first point or [Method/Knots/Object]: <point> | M | K | O
Enter next point or [start Tangency/toLerance]:
Enter next point or [end Tangency/toLerance/Undo/Close]:

parameters.name: Method (M)
parameters.description: Fit or CV. Fit passes through the points; CV uses a control polygon.

parameters.name: Knots (K)
parameters.description: Chord, Square root or Uniform parameterisation, which changes how a fit spline bulges between points.

parameters.name: Object (O)
parameters.description: Convert a spline-fit polyline (made with PEDIT Spline) into a true spline object.

parameters.name: toLerance (L)
parameters.description: Allow the curve to deviate from the fit points by up to this distance, smoothing noisy input.

parameters.name: Degree
parameters.description: In CV mode, the spline degree (commonly 3); higher degree gives smoother but less local control.

tools.example:
SPLINE
M
CV

0,0
30,40
70,-10
100,30


; Convert a smoothed polyline into a real spline
SPLINE
O
(select the polyline)
tools.notes: SPLINEDIT converts between fit and CV representations, adds or removes control points and changes the degree. SPLFRAME 1 displays the control polygon. Exporting splines to systems that only understand arcs usually requires FLATTEN or a polyline approximation.

tools.name: POINT
tools.description: Place a point object, used as a node to snap to, a surveyed coordinate, or a marker produced by DIVIDE and MEASURE. Points are invisible at the default style, so set PDMODE to a visible marker and PDSIZE to control its size before relying on them visually. Snap to them with the Node (NOD) object snap.
tools.usage:
POINT  (alias PO)
Current point modes: PDMODE=0  PDSIZE=0.0000
Specify a point: <point>

; Style is set with:
PDMODE <0-4, 32-36, 64-68, 96-100>
PDSIZE <value>   ; negative = percent of viewport

parameters.name: PDMODE
parameters.description: Point display style: 0 dot, 1 nothing, 2 cross, 3 X, 4 tick, plus 32/64/96 to add a circle, square or both.

parameters.name: PDSIZE
parameters.description: Point size. A positive value is an absolute size, a negative value is a percentage of the viewport height so points stay visible at any zoom.

parameters.name: Node osnap
parameters.description: The object snap that picks point objects; abbreviation NOD.

tools.example:
PDMODE
35
PDSIZE
-3
POINT
0,0
POINT
100,0

; Points every 10 units along a curve
MEASURE
(select curve)
10
tools.notes: Changing PDMODE or PDSIZE only updates existing points after a REGEN. DDPTYPE opens the dialog that sets both. Use DIVIDE and MEASURE to generate points along objects rather than placing them by hand.

tools.name: DONUT
tools.description: Draw a filled ring or solid-filled circle as a closed polyline made of two wide arc segments. Giving an inside diameter of 0 produces a solid dot, which is the traditional way to draw electrical connection points and solder pads in schematics. The command repeats so many donuts can be placed in one go.
tools.usage:
DONUT  (alias DO)
Specify inside diameter of donut <0.5000>: <dia>
Specify outside diameter of donut <1.0000>: <dia>
Specify center of donut or <exit>: <point> ...

parameters.name: inside diameter
parameters.description: Hole diameter; 0 makes a solid filled circle.

parameters.name: outside diameter
parameters.description: Overall diameter of the ring.

parameters.name: FILLMODE
parameters.description: System variable controlling whether the ring is displayed and plotted filled (1) or as outlines (0).

tools.example:
; Solid 2 mm connection dots at three junctions
DONUT
0
2
10,10
20,10
30,10
tools.notes: A donut is a polyline with width, so PEDIT and EXPLODE work on it normally. Set FILLMODE 0 and REGEN if filled objects slow down redraws on very large drawings.

tools.name: SOLID
tools.description: Create a filled triangle or quadrilateral 2D region (a 2D SOLID entity, not a 3D solid). It is a legacy but still useful command for quick filled shapes, section fills and arrowheads. Points are entered in a Z pattern, not around the perimeter, which is the classic trap: entering them clockwise or counter-clockwise produces a bow-tie.
tools.usage:
SOLID  (alias SO)
Specify first point: <point>
Specify second point: <point>
Specify third point: <point>      ; diagonally opposite the second
Specify fourth point or <exit>: <point> | Enter

parameters.name: point order
parameters.description: First and second points form one edge, third and fourth the opposite edge. Enter them in a Z pattern.

parameters.name: fourth point
parameters.description: Press Enter to create a filled triangle instead of a quadrilateral.

parameters.name: FILLMODE
parameters.description: Controls whether the solid displays and plots filled.

tools.example:
; Filled square using the Z order
SOLID
0,0
10,0
0,10
10,10


; Filled triangle
SOLID
20,0
30,0
25,10
tools.notes: For modern work HATCH with the SOLID pattern is usually preferable because it is associative and respects boundaries. Do not confuse this with the 3D solid primitives in the modelling toolset (BOX, CYLINDER and so on).

tools.name: HATCH
tools.description: Fill a closed area with a pattern, a solid colour or a gradient. Areas are chosen either by picking an internal point, which makes AutoCAD trace a boundary from the visible geometry, or by selecting closed objects directly. Associative hatches update automatically when their boundary is edited, which is why the pick-point method with Associative on is the normal choice.
tools.usage:
HATCH  (alias H; command-line version -HATCH)
Pick internal point or [Select objects/Undo/seTtings]:

; Command-line form used in scripts
-HATCH  Properties <pattern> <scale> <angle>  Pick internal point  Enter

parameters.name: Pattern / HPNAME
parameters.description: Pattern name such as ANSI31, SOLID, AR-CONC, NET, or a user-defined pattern from a .pat file.

parameters.name: Scale / HPSCALE
parameters.description: Pattern scale. Too small a value produces millions of lines and the 'hatch too dense' error governed by MAXHATCH and HPMAXLINES.

parameters.name: Angle / HPANG
parameters.description: Rotation of the pattern in degrees.

parameters.name: Associative
parameters.description: Links the hatch to its boundary so it updates when the boundary changes; controlled by HPASSOC.

parameters.name: Gap tolerance / HPGAPTOL
parameters.description: Largest gap in a boundary that AutoCAD will bridge when detecting an area.

parameters.name: Origin / HPORIGIN
parameters.description: Point the pattern is aligned from, important for brick and tile patterns.

parameters.name: Island detection
parameters.description: Normal, Outer or Ignore, deciding how nested closed areas are treated.

tools.example:
; Script-safe command-line hatch
FILEDIA 0
-HATCH
P
ANSI31
25
0
50,50


; AutoLISP: hatch every closed polyline on layer WALLS
(setq ss (ssget "_X" '((0 . "LWPOLYLINE") (8 . "WALLS") (70 . 1))))
(command "_-HATCH" "_P" "SOLID" "_S" ss "" "")
tools.notes: Always use -HATCH (with the leading hyphen) in scripts and macros so no dialog appears. HATCHEDIT changes an existing hatch, SETBYLAYER and DRAWORDER usually need attention afterwards, and HPLAYER can force new hatches onto a named layer regardless of the current one.

tools.name: GRADIENT
tools.description: Fill a closed area with a one- or two-colour gradient. It uses the same boundary detection and the same underlying hatch object as HATCH, so it is associative and editable with HATCHEDIT. Typical uses are presentation drawings, shaded site plans and simple rendering of elevations.
tools.usage:
GRADIENT  (alias GD; command-line version -GRADIENT)
Pick internal point or [Select objects/Undo/seTtings]:

parameters.name: One color / Two color
parameters.description: Blend a single colour towards white/black, or blend between two chosen colours.

parameters.name: Gradient pattern
parameters.description: Linear, cylindrical, inverted cylindrical, spherical, hemispherical, curved and their inverted forms.

parameters.name: Angle
parameters.description: Rotation of the gradient direction.

parameters.name: Centered
parameters.description: Whether the gradient is symmetric about the centre of the area or shifted to one side.

tools.example:
-GRADIENT
(choose options at the prompts)

; Most scripts instead set the hatch properties and use -HATCH,
; because GRADIENT shares the same underlying object:
-HATCH
P
SOLID

50,50
tools.notes: Gradient fills are hatch objects, so HATCHEDIT, DRAWORDER and transparency all apply. They can noticeably increase plot file size and rendering time on large areas.

tools.name: BOUNDARY
tools.description: Trace a closed polyline or region around an area defined by surrounding geometry, without creating a hatch. It is the standard way to get a measurable, offsettable outline from a drawing made of overlapping lines and arcs, for example to compute a floor area or to extrude a shape into a solid.
tools.usage:
BOUNDARY  (alias BO; command-line version -BOUNDARY)
(dialog) Object type: Polyline | Region
Boundary set: Current viewport | New
Island detection: on/off
Pick internal point:

parameters.name: Object type
parameters.description: Polyline (an LWPOLYLINE outline) or Region (a 2D area object suitable for MASSPROP and EXTRUDE).

parameters.name: Boundary set
parameters.description: Limit boundary detection to a selected subset of objects, which greatly speeds up detection in a busy drawing.

parameters.name: Island detection
parameters.description: Whether enclosed inner loops are included as separate boundaries.

parameters.name: Gap tolerance
parameters.description: Maximum gap that will still be treated as a closed boundary.

tools.example:
-BOUNDARY
A
I
N

O
P

100,100


; Then measure what was created
AREA
O
(select the new polyline)
tools.notes: The new outline is created on the current layer and sits exactly on top of the source geometry, so move it to a working layer immediately or it becomes impossible to select. Gaps larger than the gap tolerance cause the 'valid hatch boundary not found' error.

tools.name: REGION
tools.description: Convert closed loops of lines, polylines, arcs, circles, ellipses and splines into 2D region objects. Regions have area and mass properties, can be combined with UNION, SUBTRACT and INTERSECT, and are the usual starting point for EXTRUDE and REVOLVE when building 3D solids from 2D profiles.
tools.usage:
REGION  (alias REG)
Select objects: <selection>
Select objects: Enter
n loops extracted.  n Regions created.

parameters.name: Select objects
parameters.description: Each closed loop becomes one region; open or self-intersecting loops are rejected.

parameters.name: DELOBJ
parameters.description: System variable controlling whether the source geometry is deleted when the region is created.

tools.example:
; Plate with two holes, as a single region ready to extrude
RECTANG
0,0
100,60
CIRCLE
25,30
8
CIRCLE
75,30
8
REGION
ALL

SUBTRACT
(select the rectangle region)

(select the two circle regions)

EXTRUDE
L

10
tools.notes: MASSPROP on a region reports area, perimeter, centroid and moments of inertia, which is the quickest way to get section properties. Use BOUNDARY with Object type Region when the loops are not already separate closed objects.

tools.name: WIPEOUT
tools.description: Create an opaque polygonal area that masks everything behind it with the current background colour. It is used to clear space behind text and leaders on a busy drawing, and to blank part of an xref. The frame can be displayed for editing and hidden for plotting, which is the usual production setting.
tools.usage:
WIPEOUT
Specify first point or [Frames/Polyline] <Polyline>: <point> | F | P
Specify next point: ...

WIPEOUT  Frames  [ON/OFF/Display but not plot]

parameters.name: Polyline (P)
parameters.description: Create the wipeout from an existing closed polyline, optionally deleting the source.

parameters.name: Frames (F)
parameters.description: ON, OFF, or Display but not plot - the last is normally what production drawings want.

parameters.name: WIPEOUTFRAME
parameters.description: System variable holding the same frame setting: 0 hidden, 1 shown and plotted, 2 shown but not plotted.

tools.example:
; Mask behind a note, then hide the frame for plotting
WIPEOUT
40,40
120,40
120,60
40,60
C
DRAWORDER
L

B
WIPEOUT
F
2
tools.notes: DRAWORDER almost always has to be used after creating a wipeout, to push it behind the text it is meant to support. Wipeouts are raster-based masks: they can print as grey boxes on some older plotters and do not respect transparency.

tools.name: REVCLOUD
tools.description: Draw a revision cloud: a polyline of sequential arcs used to highlight changed areas on an issued drawing. It can be drawn freehand, as a rectangle or polygon, or converted from an existing closed object, and it can be flagged as a revision so it is easy to find and delete at the next issue.
tools.usage:
REVCLOUD
Minimum arc length: 15  Maximum arc length: 15  Style: Normal  Type: Rectangular
Specify first corner point or [Arc length/Object/Rectangular/Polygonal/Freehand/Style/Modify]:

parameters.name: Arc length (A)
parameters.description: Minimum and maximum arc length; scale these to the drawing, otherwise the cloud looks like a solid blob or a single arc.

parameters.name: Object (O)
parameters.description: Convert an existing closed object (rectangle, circle, polyline) into a revision cloud.

parameters.name: Rectangular / Polygonal / Freehand
parameters.description: How the cloud outline is defined.

parameters.name: Style (S)
parameters.description: Normal or Calligraphy, the latter giving a variable-width pen look.

parameters.name: Modify (M)
parameters.description: Add to or remove a side from an existing revision cloud.

tools.example:
REVCLOUD
A
150
300

R
1000,1000
2500,1800

; Convert an existing rectangle into a cloud
REVCLOUD
O
(select rectangle)
N
tools.notes: REVCLOUDPROPERTIES and the REVCLOUDCREATEMODE / REVCLOUDARCVARIANCE system variables control the defaults. Because the cloud is an ordinary polyline it can be put on a dedicated REVISION layer and frozen when the revision is superseded.

tools.name: TEXT
tools.description: Create single-line text objects. Each line is a separate object, which makes it ideal for labels, schedules filled by scripts and any text that will be read back by LISP, because entget returns the string directly in DXF group 1. The command stays active after each line so several labels can be typed in sequence.
tools.usage:
TEXT  (alias DT; also DTEXT)
Specify start point of text or [Justify/Style]: <point> | J | S
Specify height <2.5000>: <height>
Specify rotation angle of text <0>: <angle>
Enter text: <string>

parameters.name: Justify (J)
parameters.description: Align, Fit, Center, Middle, Right, TL/TC/TR, ML/MC/MR, BL/BC/BR.

parameters.name: Style (S)
parameters.description: Choose a text style defined with STYLE; the style may fix the height, in which case the height prompt is skipped.

parameters.name: height
parameters.description: Text height in drawing units. Annotative styles ask for the paper height instead.

parameters.name: rotation angle
parameters.description: Rotation in degrees from the current UCS X axis.

tools.example:
TEXT
J
MC
100,50
5
0
PUMP ROOM


; AutoLISP: create text directly without the command prompt
(entmake (list '(0 . "TEXT")
               '(100 . "AcDbEntity") '(8 . "NOTES")
               '(100 . "AcDbText")
               '(10 100.0 50.0 0.0)
               '(40 . 5.0)
               '(1 . "PUMP ROOM")))
tools.notes: Use MTEXT for paragraphs, formatting and word wrap. TEXTEDIT (or double-click) edits existing text; TEXTSIZE holds the default height. Special codes %%d, %%c and %%p produce the degree, diameter and plus/minus symbols.

tools.name: MTEXT
tools.description: Create a multiline paragraph text object inside a defined width, with word wrap, mixed fonts, bold and italic, stacked fractions, bullets and numbering, columns and embedded fields. It is the right choice for general notes, specifications and anything that needs formatting, and it counts as one object however many lines it contains.
tools.usage:
MTEXT  (alias T or MT; command-line version -MTEXT)
Specify first corner: <point>
Specify opposite corner or [Height/Justify/Line spacing/Rotation/Style/Width/Columns]: <point>
(opens the in-place text editor)

parameters.name: Height (H)
parameters.description: Text height; with an annotative style this is the paper height.

parameters.name: Justify (J)
parameters.description: TL, TC, TR, ML, MC, MR, BL, BC, BR - attachment point of the text frame.

parameters.name: Line spacing (L)
parameters.description: At least or Exactly, with a spacing factor.

parameters.name: Width (W)
parameters.description: Wrap width; 0 means no wrapping.

parameters.name: Columns (C)
parameters.description: Dynamic or static columns with a set height and gutter.

parameters.name: Style (S)
parameters.description: Text style to use, defined with STYLE.

tools.example:
; Command-line version, safe in scripts
-MTEXT
10,10
H
3.5
J
TL
W
80
1. ALL DIMENSIONS IN MILLIMETRES.
2. WELD ALL ROUND UNLESS NOTED.


; Insert a field that tracks the drawing name
; (type inside the MTEXT editor, or use FIELD)
tools.notes: MTEXTED and MTEXTTOOLBAR control which editor appears. Use -MTEXT in scripts because the normal command opens an in-place editor that scripts cannot drive. TXT2MTXT converts a set of single-line TEXT objects into one MTEXT.

tools.name: TABLE
tools.description: Insert a table object with rows, columns, a title and header, formatted by a table style. Cells can hold text, blocks, formulas that reference other cells, and fields that read drawing properties or sheet-set data. A table can also be linked to an Excel range with DATALINK so the drawing updates when the spreadsheet changes.
tools.usage:
TABLE  (alias TB; command-line version -TABLE)
(dialog) Table style / Insert options / Column & row settings / Cell styles
Specify insertion point:

parameters.name: Table style
parameters.description: Named style created with TABLESTYLE, controlling text styles, colours, borders and cell margins.

parameters.name: Columns / Column width
parameters.description: Number of columns and their width in drawing units.

parameters.name: Data rows / Row height
parameters.description: Number of data rows and their height in text line units.

parameters.name: From a data link
parameters.description: Build the table from an Excel range defined with DATALINK, keeping it synchronised.

parameters.name: From object data
parameters.description: Build the table from a data extraction (DATAEXTRACTION) of block attributes and object properties.

tools.example:
-TABLE
4
8


200,150

; Insert a formula in a cell (in the in-place editor): =SUM(A2:A7)

; Link a table to a spreadsheet instead
DATALINK
(create a link to the .xlsx range)
TABLE
(choose 'From a data link')
tools.notes: TABLEDIT edits cell contents, TABLESTYLE defines the appearance and TABLEEXPORT writes the table out as CSV. Tables inserted from a data link are updated with DATALINKUPDATE.

tools.name: BLOCK
tools.description: Define a block: a named collection of objects stored inside the drawing that can be inserted many times as a single object. Blocks are the foundation of reuse in AutoCAD - symbols, title blocks, furniture, fasteners - and updating the definition updates every insertion. The base point chosen here becomes the insertion point of every INSERT.
tools.usage:
BLOCK  (alias B; command-line version -BLOCK)
(dialog) Name / Base point / Objects (Retain, Convert to block, Delete) / Block unit / Description

-BLOCK
Enter block name or [?]: <name>
Specify insertion base point: <point>
Select objects: <selection>

parameters.name: Name
parameters.description: Block name. A leading asterisk makes it anonymous; names beginning with a dollar are reserved for AutoCAD's own anonymous blocks.

parameters.name: Base point
parameters.description: Insertion point of the block, best placed at a meaningful feature such as a corner or centre.

parameters.name: Objects behaviour
parameters.description: Retain the source objects, convert them to a block reference in place, or delete them.

parameters.name: Block unit
parameters.description: Unit the block is drawn in; combined with INSUNITS it scales the block automatically when inserted into a drawing with different units.

parameters.name: Allow exploding / Scale uniformly
parameters.description: Flags stored in the definition that restrict how insertions can be modified.

tools.example:
; Command-line form for scripts
-BLOCK
VALVE_GATE
0,0
ALL


; Redefine an existing block from new geometry
-BLOCK
VALVE_GATE
Y
0,0
(select new geometry)
tools.notes: Redefining a block updates every insertion in the drawing immediately. Draw block geometry on layer 0 with colour and linetype ByBlock if it should inherit the properties of the layer it is inserted on. BEDIT opens the Block Editor for dynamic blocks; WBLOCK writes a block out to its own DWG file.

tools.name: INSERT
tools.description: Place a block reference in the drawing, from a block already defined here or from an external DWG file. Scale and rotation can be set at insertion, and an existing definition can be redefined from a file by inserting it with an equals sign. In AutoCAD 2020 and later the ribbon Insert command opens the Blocks palette; -INSERT remains the command-line form that scripts use.
tools.usage:
INSERT  (alias I; command-line version -INSERT)
-INSERT
Enter block name or [?] <last>: <name> | <path\file.dwg> | <name>=<path\file.dwg>
Specify insertion point or [Basepoint/Scale/X/Y/Z/Rotate/PScale/PX/PY/PZ/PRotate]:
Enter X scale factor: / Y scale factor: / rotation angle:

parameters.name: name=path
parameters.description: Redefine the block from an external file, updating every existing insertion. The standard way to roll out a revised title block.

parameters.name: Scale (S) / X / Y / Z
parameters.description: Uniform or per-axis scale factors; negative values mirror the block.

parameters.name: Rotate (R)
parameters.description: Rotation angle at insertion.

parameters.name: *name
parameters.description: Prefixing the name with an asterisk inserts the block already exploded into its component objects.

parameters.name: ATTDIA / ATTREQ
parameters.description: Control whether attribute values are prompted for in a dialog, at the command line, or not at all.

tools.example:
ATTDIA 0
ATTREQ 1
-INSERT
TITLEBLOCK_A1=C:/standards/blocks/TB_A1.dwg
0,0
1
1
0
PROJECT 1042
REV C

; Insert pre-exploded
-INSERT
*VALVE_GATE
100,50
1
0
tools.notes: Set ATTDIA 0 before scripted insertion of blocks with attributes, otherwise a dialog stops the script. INSUNITS on both drawings controls automatic unit scaling; mismatched units are the usual cause of blocks arriving 25.4 times too big or small.

tools.name: WBLOCK
tools.description: Write objects, an existing block definition or the entire drawing out to a separate DWG file. It is the standard way to build a block library from geometry already drawn, and the Entire drawing option is also the classic way to shed accumulated junk from a corrupted or bloated file because only referenced objects are written.
tools.usage:
WBLOCK  (alias W; command-line version -WBLOCK)
(dialog) Source: Block | Entire drawing | Objects
Base point / Objects / Destination file name and path / Insert units

-WBLOCK
Enter name of output file: <path>
Enter name of existing block or [= (block=output file)/* (whole drawing)] <define new drawing>:

parameters.name: Source: Block
parameters.description: Write an existing block definition out to a file of its own.

parameters.name: Source: Entire drawing
parameters.description: Write the whole drawing, omitting unreferenced definitions - an effective cleanup.

parameters.name: Source: Objects
parameters.description: Write a selection set, with a chosen base point, to a new file.

parameters.name: Insert units
parameters.description: Unit the resulting file is tagged with, used for automatic scaling on insertion.

tools.example:
; Export a selection to a library file
FILEDIA 0
-WBLOCK
C:/standards/blocks/VALVE_GATE.dwg

0,0
(select objects)


; Export an existing block definition
-WBLOCK
C:/standards/blocks/TB_A1.dwg
TITLEBLOCK_A1
tools.notes: Set FILEDIA 0 before -WBLOCK in scripts so the file dialog is suppressed. The base point chosen becomes the origin of the new drawing, so pick it deliberately. PURGE and AUDIT are the gentler alternatives for cleaning a drawing.

tools.name: ATTDEF
tools.description: Define an attribute: a text placeholder inside a block definition that carries a tag, a prompt and a value. Attributes turn a block into a data carrier - part numbers, room names, title-block fields, equipment tags - and their values can be extracted to a table or spreadsheet with DATAEXTRACTION. Define them before running BLOCK and include them in the selection set.
tools.usage:
ATTDEF  (alias ATT; command-line version -ATTDEF)
(dialog) Mode: Invisible / Constant / Verify / Preset / Lock position / Multiple lines
Attribute: Tag / Prompt / Default
Text settings: Justification / Style / Height / Rotation / Annotative
Insertion point:

parameters.name: Tag
parameters.description: Internal name of the attribute, uppercase without spaces. This is what DATAEXTRACTION and LISP see.

parameters.name: Prompt
parameters.description: Question shown to the user when the block is inserted.

parameters.name: Default
parameters.description: Initial value, which may be a field expression.

parameters.name: Invisible
parameters.description: Value is stored but not displayed; used for hidden data such as manufacturer codes.

parameters.name: Constant
parameters.description: Value is fixed in the definition and cannot be changed per insertion.

parameters.name: Preset
parameters.description: Uses the default without prompting, but the value can still be edited afterwards.

parameters.name: Verify
parameters.description: Asks the user to confirm the value after entry.

tools.example:
-ATTDEF

TAG_NO
Equipment tag number:
P-000
0,0
2.5
0

; Then build the block including the attribute
-BLOCK
EQUIP_TAG
0,0
ALL


; Edit values later
EATTEDIT   ; single reference
BATTMAN    ; manage the definition's attributes
tools.notes: Attribute order in the insertion prompt follows the selection order when the block was made; BATTMAN reorders them. ATTSYNC pushes definition changes out to existing insertions. ATTDISP controls global visibility of all attributes.

tools.name: BASE
tools.description: Set the insertion base point of the current drawing, which is the point that lands on the insertion point when this drawing is inserted into another as a block or attached as an external reference. It defaults to the origin, and getting it right matters for title blocks, standard details and xref-based workflows.
tools.usage:
BASE
Enter base point <0.0000,0.0000,0.0000>: <point>

; Stored in the INSBASE system variable

parameters.name: base point
parameters.description: Coordinate in the current UCS that becomes the drawing's insertion point.

parameters.name: INSBASE
parameters.description: System variable holding the same value; readable and writable with getvar/setvar.

tools.example:
; Make the lower-left corner of the sheet the insertion point
BASE
0,0,0

; From AutoLISP
(setvar "INSBASE" (list 0.0 0.0 0.0))
(princ (getvar "INSBASE"))
tools.notes: Changing BASE does not move existing insertions of the drawing; it only affects future INSERT and XATTACH operations. For blocks defined inside the drawing, the base point is set in BLOCK instead.

tools.name: MLINE
tools.description: Draw a multiline: up to sixteen parallel lines drawn in one operation as a single object, with per-element offsets, colours and linetypes, and optional end caps and a fill. It is the traditional tool for walls, roads and cable trays in plain AutoCAD, where a wall needs two or three parallel lines that stay together.
tools.usage:
MLINE  (alias ML)
Current settings: Justification = Top, Scale = 20.00, Style = STANDARD
Specify start point or [Justification/Scale/STyle]: <point> | J | S | ST

parameters.name: Justification (J)
parameters.description: Top, Zero or Bottom - which element of the multiline follows the points you pick.

parameters.name: Scale (S)
parameters.description: Multiplier applied to the element offsets defined in the style; for a 200 mm wall from a style with offsets 0.5/-0.5, use scale 200.

parameters.name: STyle (ST)
parameters.description: Named multiline style created with MLSTYLE.

parameters.name: Close (C)
parameters.description: Close the multiline back to the start point with a proper mitred joint.

tools.example:
MLSTYLE
(create a style with elements at +0.5 and -0.5)

MLINE
J
Z
S
200
ST
WALL
0,0
5000,0
5000,4000
0,4000
C
tools.notes: MLEDIT handles the junctions (crosses, tees, corner joints) that MLINE itself cannot resolve. Multilines cannot be offset or trimmed like normal lines and many offices prefer plain polylines instead; exploding an MLINE converts it to individual lines.

tools.name: MLSTYLE
tools.description: Create and edit multiline styles: the number of parallel elements, their offsets, colours and linetypes, the start and end caps (line, outer arc, inner arc, angled), the fill colour and whether joints are displayed. A style must exist before MLINE can draw anything other than the two-element STANDARD.
tools.usage:
MLSTYLE
(dialog) Styles list / New / Modify / Rename / Delete / Load / Save
Element properties: Offset, Color, Linetype
Multiline properties: Display joints, Caps (line/outer arc/inner arc/angle), Fill

parameters.name: Offset
parameters.description: Distance of each element from the multiline's zero line, later multiplied by the MLINE scale.

parameters.name: Caps
parameters.description: Line, outer arc, inner arc or an angled cap at the start and end of the multiline.

parameters.name: Fill
parameters.description: Solid background colour between the outermost elements, useful for poche walls.

parameters.name: Load / Save
parameters.description: Read and write style definitions to an .mln file so they can be shared between drawings.

tools.example:
MLSTYLE
(New: WALL_200)
(Elements: 0.5 ByLayer ByLayer, -0.5 ByLayer ByLayer)
(Caps: line at start and end)
(Save to C:/standards/office.mln)

MLINE
ST
WALL_200
S
200
J
Z
0,0
5000,0
tools.notes: The STANDARD style cannot be renamed or deleted and its elements cannot be changed once multilines using it exist. Styles are stored in the drawing; use Save/Load with an .mln file to move them between drawings.

tools.name: SKETCH
tools.description: Draw freehand by following the pointing device, recording a stream of short segments as lines, polylines or splines. It is a niche command today but remains the way to trace scanned drawings, capture contour lines and record signature-like geometry. The record increment controls how finely the motion is sampled.
tools.usage:
SKETCH
Type = Lines  Increment = 1.0000  Tolerance = 0.5000
Specify sketch or [Type/Increment/toLerance]: T | I | L | <drag>

parameters.name: Type (T)
parameters.description: Line, Polyline or Spline - what the recorded motion is converted into. SKPOLY holds the same setting.

parameters.name: Increment (I)
parameters.description: Minimum distance the cursor must move before a new segment is recorded; smaller values give more detail and far more objects.

parameters.name: toLerance (L)
parameters.description: Spline fit tolerance when Type is Spline.

parameters.name: SKETCHINC
parameters.description: System variable holding the record increment.

tools.example:
SKETCH
T
P

I
2

(drag the pointer to trace the contour)
(press Enter to record and exit)
tools.notes: A small increment on a large trace can create tens of thousands of objects and bloat the drawing; check with the object count afterwards and consider OVERKILL or a spline conversion. SKPOLY 1 makes sketches polylines rather than individual lines.

tools.name: HELIX
tools.description: Draw a 2D spiral or 3D helix from a base centre, base radius, top radius and height, with a given number of turns and turn direction. Its main use is as the path for SWEEP when modelling springs, threads and spiral stairs; a helix with zero height is a flat spiral.
tools.usage:
HELIX
Number of turns = 3.0000  Twist = CCW
Specify center point of base: <point>
Specify base radius or [Diameter] <1.0000>:
Specify top radius or [Diameter] <base>:
Specify helix height or [Axis endpoint/Turns/turn Height/tWist]:

parameters.name: Turns (T)
parameters.description: Number of revolutions; maximum 500.

parameters.name: turn Height (H)
parameters.description: Pitch - the height of a single turn. Setting it derives the total height from the turn count.

parameters.name: tWist (W)
parameters.description: CW or CCW winding direction.

parameters.name: Axis endpoint (A)
parameters.description: Define the helix axis direction and length by a point, allowing a helix at any orientation.

parameters.name: top radius
parameters.description: Different from the base radius gives a conical (tapered) helix.

tools.example:
; Compression spring: 20 mm coil diameter, 60 mm long, 8 turns, 2 mm wire
HELIX
0,0,0
10
10
T
8
60

CIRCLE
10,0,0
1

SWEEP
L

(select the helix as the path)
tools.notes: SWEEP with a helix path needs the profile positioned at the helix start point and perpendicular to it; the Alignment option of SWEEP handles the rest. A helix is a spline-based path object, not a solid.

tools.name: 3DPOLY
tools.description: Draw a polyline whose vertices can have different Z values, producing a genuinely three-dimensional path. Unlike PLINE it accepts only straight segments and has no width, but it is the object to use for survey strings, pipe centrelines, cable routes and any SWEEP or EXTRUDE path that leaves a single plane.
tools.usage:
3DPOLY  (alias 3P)
Specify start point of polyline: <x,y,z>
Specify endpoint of line or [Undo]: <x,y,z>
Specify endpoint of line or [Close/Undo]: C | U | Enter

parameters.name: Close (C)
parameters.description: Close the 3D polyline back to its start point.

parameters.name: Undo (U)
parameters.description: Remove the last segment without leaving the command.

parameters.name: x,y,z
parameters.description: Full 3D coordinates; @dx,dy,dz gives relative 3D movement.

tools.example:
; Pipe centreline rising through three levels
3DPOLY
0,0,0
5000,0,0
5000,0,3000
5000,4000,3000


; Sweep a circle along it
CIRCLE
0,0,0
50
SWEEP
L

(select the 3D polyline)
tools.notes: PEDIT can spline-fit a 3D polyline into a smooth 3D curve. A 3D polyline cannot have arc segments, width or linetype generation; convert to a spline if a smooth path is needed. FLATTEN or the Z coordinate of each vertex can be edited in the Properties palette.

tools.name: DIVIDE
tools.description: Place point objects or block references at equally spaced intervals along an object, dividing it into a given number of equal parts. The object itself is not cut - only markers are placed. It is the quickest way to set out bolt holes on an arc, fence posts along a boundary or stations along a centreline.
tools.usage:
DIVIDE  (alias DIV)
Select object to divide: <object>
Enter the number of segments or [Block]: <n> | B
(Block) Enter name of block to insert:
Align block with object? [Yes/No] <Y>:

parameters.name: number of segments
parameters.description: Number of equal parts; n-1 markers are placed because the ends are not marked.

parameters.name: Block (B)
parameters.description: Insert a named block at each division point instead of a point object.

parameters.name: Align block with object
parameters.description: Yes rotates each block to follow the tangent of the curve at that point.

tools.example:
PDMODE
35
; Eight equal divisions along an arc
DIVIDE
(select arc)
8

; Fence posts as blocks, aligned to the boundary
DIVIDE
(select polyline)
B
FENCE_POST
Y
12
tools.notes: Set PDMODE to a visible style before using DIVIDE with points, or nothing appears to happen. Use the Node object snap to pick the resulting points. MEASURE is the companion command that spaces markers at a fixed distance instead of an equal count.

tools.name: MEASURE
tools.description: Place point objects or blocks at a fixed interval along an object, starting from the end nearest the pick point. Any remainder is left at the far end, which is exactly the behaviour wanted for setting out sleepers, studs, rebar or chainage marks at a specified spacing.
tools.usage:
MEASURE  (alias ME)
Select object to measure: <object>
Specify length of segment or [Block]: <dist> | B
(Block) Enter name of block to insert:
Align block with object? [Yes/No] <Y>:

parameters.name: length of segment
parameters.description: Fixed distance between markers, measured along the object.

parameters.name: Block (B)
parameters.description: Place a named block at each interval instead of a point.

parameters.name: Align block with object
parameters.description: Yes rotates each inserted block to the tangent direction of the curve.

parameters.name: pick point
parameters.description: Measuring starts from the end of the object nearest where you picked it, so pick deliberately.

tools.example:
PDMODE
34
; Chainage marks every 25 m along an alignment
MEASURE
(select the polyline near its start)
25000

; Studs every 600 mm along a wall line
MEASURE
(select line)
B
STUD_90
Y
600
tools.notes: Markers are separate objects, not associated with the source; editing the source does not move them. Combine with a temporary layer so the whole set can be deleted in one go once the setting-out is done.

tools.name: MLEADER
tools.description: Create a multileader: a leader line with one or more landing segments, an arrowhead and content that is either MTEXT or a block. Multileaders are style-driven, can be collected into a group with MLEADERCOLLECT, aligned with MLEADERALIGN and given extra leader lines later, which makes them the modern replacement for LEADER and QLEADER.
tools.usage:
MLEADER  (alias MLD)
Specify leader arrowhead location or [leader Landing first/Content first/Options] <Options>:
Specify leader landing location:
(then enter the MTEXT content or choose the block)

parameters.name: leader Landing first (L)
parameters.description: Pick the landing (text) end before the arrow end.

parameters.name: Content first (C)
parameters.description: Enter the text or block first and then place the leader.

parameters.name: Options (O)
parameters.description: Leader type (straight, spline, none), landing settings, content type, maximum leader points, first and second segment angles.

parameters.name: Multileader style
parameters.description: Named style from MLEADERSTYLE controlling arrowhead, landing gap, text style and scale.

tools.example:
MLEADERSTYLE
(create style NOTE_3.5 with a closed filled arrow and 3.5 text)

MLEADER
100,100
140,130
SEE DETAIL 4/A-201


; Add a second arrow to the same multileader
MLEADEREDIT
(select the multileader)
A
80,90

; Tidy a column of notes
MLEADERALIGN
tools.notes: MLEADEREDIT adds and removes leader lines, MLEADERCOLLECT merges block-content multileaders into one, and MLEADERALIGN lines up a set of them. Annotative multileader styles scale automatically with the viewport annotation scale.

tools.name: LEADER
tools.description: Draw a legacy leader line with an arrowhead and optional annotation, which may be text, a tolerance frame, a block reference or a copy of an existing annotation object. It predates MLEADER and is kept for compatibility and for the cases where a leader must be associated with a dimension style rather than a multileader style.
tools.usage:
LEADER  (alias LEAD)
Specify leader start point: <point>
Specify next point: <point>
Specify next point or [Annotation/Format/Undo] <Annotation>: A | F | U
Annotation options: [Tolerance/Copy/Block/None/Mtext]

parameters.name: Annotation (A)
parameters.description: Attach content: Mtext, a Tolerance frame, a Copy of an existing annotation, a Block, or None.

parameters.name: Format (F)
parameters.description: Spline or STraight leader line, and whether an ARrow or None is drawn at the start.

parameters.name: Undo (U)
parameters.description: Remove the last leader vertex.

parameters.name: dimension style
parameters.description: LEADER takes its arrowhead, text style and scale from the current dimension style (DIMSTYLE), not from a multileader style.

tools.example:
LEADER
100,100
140,130

A

GRIND FLUSH


; QLEADER with a preconfigured setup is the usual legacy shortcut
QLEADER
S
(set annotation type and attachment in the dialog)
tools.notes: Prefer MLEADER for new work: it is style-driven, supports multiple leaders per note and can be aligned and collected. QLEADER is the settings-driven variant of this command and is still widely used in older office standards.

tools.name: GEOMCONSTRAINT
tools.description: Apply a geometric constraint between objects so the sketch keeps a relationship as it is edited: coincident, collinear, concentric, parallel, perpendicular, horizontal, vertical, tangent, smooth, symmetric, equal or fix. Geometric constraints are the first half of parametric drawing; dimensional constraints supply the sizes.
tools.usage:
GEOMCONSTRAINT
Enter constraint type [Horizontal/Vertical/Perpendicular/PArallel/Tangent/SMooth/Coincident/CONcentric/COLlinear/Symmetric/Equal/Fix] <Coincident>:
Select object / Select first object, second object:

parameters.name: Coincident
parameters.description: Make two points, or a point and an object, coincide. The most common constraint in any sketch.

parameters.name: Parallel / Perpendicular / Tangent
parameters.description: Relationship between two lines or a line and a curve.

parameters.name: Concentric
parameters.description: Force two circles, arcs or ellipses to share a centre.

parameters.name: Fix
parameters.description: Anchor a point or object in place so the rest of the sketch moves relative to it.

parameters.name: Equal / Symmetric
parameters.description: Force equal length or radius, or mirror symmetry about a line.

parameters.name: CONSTRAINTBAR
parameters.description: Command that shows or hides the constraint bars marking which constraints are applied.

tools.example:
; Constrain a rough rectangle into a true one
GEOMCONSTRAINT
H
(select bottom line)
GEOMCONSTRAINT
V
(select left line)
GEOMCONSTRAINT
PA
(select bottom line)
(select top line)
GEOMCONSTRAINT
F
(select lower-left corner)

AUTOCONSTRAIN
ALL
tools.notes: AUTOCONSTRAIN applies a whole set of constraints automatically based on the current geometry and tolerances. DELCONSTRAINT removes them. Over-constraining produces an error rather than silently moving geometry, so build up constraints gradually.

tools.name: DIMCONSTRAINT
tools.description: Apply a dimensional constraint that drives the size of geometry: linear, horizontal, vertical, aligned, angular, radial, diameter, or a conversion of an existing associative dimension into a constraint. The value can be a number or an expression referencing other constraint parameters, which is how a parametric block or detail is built.
tools.usage:
DIMCONSTRAINT  (alias DCON)
Enter constraint type [Linear/Horizontal/Vertical/Aligned/ANgular/Radial/Diameter/Form/Convert] <Aligned>:
Select object / points, then place the dimension and accept or edit the expression

parameters.name: Linear / Horizontal / Vertical / Aligned
parameters.description: Distance constraints between points or along an object.

parameters.name: ANgular / Radial / Diameter
parameters.description: Angle, radius and diameter constraints.

parameters.name: Convert (C)
parameters.description: Turn an existing associative dimension into a dimensional constraint that now drives the geometry.

parameters.name: Form (F)
parameters.description: Switch new constraints between Dynamic (display only at edit time) and Annotational (plotted like a normal dimension).

parameters.name: expression
parameters.description: A constraint value can be an expression such as d1*2 or width/3, referencing other parameters listed in the Parameters Manager.

tools.example:
DIMCONSTRAINT
H
(pick two points)
(place dimension)
width=200

DIMCONSTRAINT
V
(pick two points)
(place dimension)
height=width/2

PARAMETERS
; change width to 300 and the geometry updates
tools.notes: Dynamic constraints are display-only and do not plot; Annotational constraints look and plot like dimensions. DELCONSTRAINT removes constraints, and the Parameters Manager (PARAMETERS) is where expressions and user parameters are managed.

tools.name: AUTOCONSTRAIN
tools.description: Apply geometric constraints automatically to a selection, inferring coincidence, parallelism, perpendicularity, tangency, concentricity and horizontal/vertical alignment from the existing geometry within a distance and angle tolerance. It is the fast way to turn an already-drawn shape into a constrained sketch instead of applying dozens of constraints by hand.
tools.usage:
AUTOCONSTRAIN
Select objects or [Settings]: <selection> | S
(Settings dialog) constraint types to apply, their priority order, tolerances

parameters.name: Settings (S)
parameters.description: Choose which constraint types are applied and in what priority order, and set the distance and angle tolerances.

parameters.name: Tolerances
parameters.description: How close geometry must be before a constraint is inferred - too loose and unwanted constraints appear.

parameters.name: CONSTRAINTINFER
parameters.description: System variable that makes AutoCAD infer constraints continuously while drawing, rather than after the fact.

tools.example:
AUTOCONSTRAIN
S
(clear Tangent and Symmetric, set distance tolerance 0.05)

ALL

CONSTRAINTBAR
ALL

; Then add the driving dimensions
DIMCONSTRAINT
H
(pick the width)
width=200
tools.notes: Run it on a clean, well-drawn shape: sloppy geometry produces a tangle of constraints that then fight each other. DELCONSTRAINT with the All option clears everything and lets you start again.

tools.name: PARAMETERS
tools.description: Open the Parameters Manager palette, which lists every dimensional constraint and user parameter in the drawing with its name, expression and current value. User parameters can be created here and referenced from constraint expressions, turning a constrained sketch into a driven model where changing one number updates the whole shape.
tools.usage:
PARAMETERS  (close with PARAMETERSCLOSE)
(palette) Name / Expression / Value, grouped into Dimensional Constraint Parameters and User Parameters

parameters.name: Name
parameters.description: Parameter name used in expressions; rename the automatic d1, d2 names to meaningful ones such as width and bore.

parameters.name: Expression
parameters.description: A number or a formula referencing other parameters and functions, e.g. width/2 or bore*1.5+3.

parameters.name: User Parameters
parameters.description: Named values that do not drive geometry directly but can be referenced by constraint expressions.

parameters.name: Filters
parameters.description: Group parameters so a complex parametric block stays manageable.

tools.example:
PARAMETERS
; Create a user parameter
;   wall_t = 200
; Then drive constraints from it
DIMCONSTRAINT
H
(pick the wall thickness)
thickness=wall_t

; Changing wall_t to 250 updates every constraint that references it
tools.notes: Expressions support the usual arithmetic plus functions such as sin, cos, atan, sqrt, round and abs, with angles in degrees. In a dynamic block the same manager appears inside the Block Editor (BPARAMETER and BEDIT) and drives block actions.
